evidence_spans: In the present work, we used in situ scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), corroborated with atomistic simulations, to study in real‐time and at the atomic scale the structural and compositional evolution of AuCoCuNiPt NPs from 298 to 973 K.

cross_paper_synthesis.consensus: High-entropy nanoalloys (HENAs) of AuCoCuNiPt predominantly form multi-twinned structures rather than equilibrium Wulff shapes in the as-deposited sub-10 nm regime, and chemical segregation becomes size-dependent during heating, with larger particles (>5 nm) showing frequent phase separation into Au-Cu rich domains.
cross_paper_synthesis.different_approaches: The evidence distinguishes between as-deposited structural stability and heating-induced evolution. While as-deposited particles are characterized by a homogenous elemental distribution despite high defect densities (multi-twinned), heating induces distinct morphological and compositional changes, including the formation of surface AuCu layers and phase separation in larger coalesced particles.
cross_paper_synthesis.condition_dependencies: The formation of multi-twinned structures is the dominant regime for sub-10 nm particles (answer_id: PMC11775865::reader_question::b612426a709dbfea::answer::28ba189fbac73b15). Phase separation is strictly condition-dependent on size, occurring frequently in particles >5 nm during coalescence but remaining unobserved or unexplained for smaller particles (answer_id: PMC11775865::reader_question::85ed0f3cb35927d4::answer::24ad21e2ac17e1c3).
cross_paper_synthesis.contradictions: There are no direct contradictions in the data; however, there is an apparent tension between the observation of 'homogenous distribution' of five metals in multi-twinned structures and the simultaneous observation of high defect density, as the text does not mechanistically explain if segregation is occurring at twin boundaries (answer_id: PMC11775865::reader_question::17481b4c322728db::answer::71155d6c460eddf1).
cross_paper_synthesis.evidence_strength: Strong observational evidence exists for structural motifs and phase separation thresholds (answer_id: PMC11775865::reader_question::85ed0f3cb35927d4::answer::24ad21e2ac17e1c3, answer_id: PMC11775865::reader_question::b612426a709dbfea::answer::28ba189fbac73b15). Weaker evidence exists regarding the thermodynamic drivers, as the text provides no numerical values for standard deviation or explicit energetic comparisons to confirm negligible segregation (answer_id: PMC11775865::reader_question::7ed17339af4e8a67::answer::70feb96bba1c0397) or the specific nature of the AuCu layer (answer_id: PMC11775865::reader_question::830afe415d821604::answer::6244d57703092a66).
cross_paper_synthesis.unresolved_gap: The specific mechanism distinguishing the 'AuCu layer' from general segregation, the location of non-Au-Cu components during coalescence (core vs. interface), and the theoretical size threshold where surface energy dominance shifts from favoring Wulff shapes to multi-twinned structures remain unquantified.
cross_paper_synthesis.candidate_hypothesis: Below the 5 nm coalescence threshold, high surface energy and kinetic trapping in multi-twinned structures suppress phase separation, maintaining apparent homogeneity, whereas above this threshold, surface diffusion drives Au-Cu segregation into distinct intermetallic phases while larger volumes allow thermodynamic phase separation.
cross_paper_synthesis.discriminating_experiment: Perform atomic-resolution STEM-EDS line scans across twin boundaries in sub-5 nm particles at elevated temperatures (773 K) to detect if the 'homogenous distribution' holds at the atomic scale or if segregation is confined to defects, and measure the standard deviation of composition in Figure 1c with high-precision statistics to verify the assumption of negligible segregation.
